title: The Cult of the Child Prodigy: Why Pushing Kids into the Competitive Rat Race Backfires

linkedin.hook: 70% of kids quit organized sports by age 13. Not because they lack talent. Because their parents turned childhood into a performance review.
linkedin.body:
When did childhood become an entry-level corporate internship?

If you observe the modern suburban family calendar, free play has been replaced by calendar blocks. Sandboxes have been replaced by competitive tutoring centers.

We tell ourselves we're giving them a 'head start.'

In economics, Goodhart's Law states: 'When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure.'

When we turn trophies, grades, and Ivy League percentiles into the explicit target:

1. Intrinsic curiosity dies (Deci & Ryan, Self-Determination Theory).
2. Children become 'teacups'—flawless on paper, but shattering at the first taste of real-world friction.
3. They become external-validation junkies.

As Dr. Alison Gopnik writes: Be a Gardener, not a Carpenter.

A carpenter tries to chisel raw wood into a specific chair. A gardener enriches the soil, provides safety and sunlight, and allows a unique, resilient ecosystem to grow.

In an AI-accelerated future, the winners won't be the kids who memorized the rubric fastest at age 8. They will be the ones who learned how to be bored, tinker, fail, and think for themselves.

Read the full deep-dive with research citations: https://mjidea.pages.dev/ideas/kids-pushed-to-race-by-parents

#Parenting #ChildPsychology #Humanity #Leadership #FutureOfEducation
linkedin.cta: What's one thing you did as a child with ZERO adult supervision that shaped who you are today?

thread:
1/ 70% of children quit competitive sports by age 13.

Adolescent anxiety in high-achieving schools has doubled.

Why? Because modern parents turned childhood into a high-stakes corporate internship 🧵👇

2/ Charles Goodhart's Law in the living room:

'When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure.'

When grades and trophies become the only target, intrinsic curiosity is extinguished. Kids stop learning for joy and start performing for parental approval.

3/ Dr. Alison Gopnik's framework:

🔨 The Carpenter Parent: Tries to chisel the child into an engineered resume.

🌱 The Gardener Parent: Enriches the soil, protects the perimeter, and lets the unique plant grow deep roots.

Carpenters build fragile kids. Gardeners grow antifragile adults.

4/ The 50-year Play Deficit:

Since 1950, unsupervised free play has dropped 70%. In that exact same window, youth anxiety quadrupled.

Unsupervised play is where kids learn conflict resolution, emotional self-regulation, and internal locus of control.

5/ The operational fix:

• Protect empty calendar blocks (boredom breeds creativity)
• Praise effort and autonomy, never the scoreboard
• Let them fail early without rescuing them

Full essay with AAP & Harvard research: https://mjidea.pages.dev/ideas/kids-pushed-to-race-by-parents
